body:
> ⚠️ **Preliminary analysis (low confidence)** — treat as a starting point, not a conclusion.

I think the Workspaces list keeps stale row positions after you create a workspace. The list is a FlashList v2 in [`src/components/Table/TableBody.tsx:459-512`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/src/components/Table/TableBody.tsx#L459-L512). It places each row with `position: absolute` and a `top` value calculated from the row heights it measured earlier.

This is how the rows could end up overlapping:

1. When you confirm the new workspace, the app opens that workspace's pages, so the Workspaces list is hidden (`display: none`, size 0x0).
2. The local patch [`@shopify+flash-list+2.3.2+002+skip-layout-when-hidden.patch:5-23`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/patches/@shopify/flash-list/@shopify+flash-list+2.3.2+002+skip-layout-when-hidden.patch#L5-L23) skips all measuring while the list is 0x0. The new workspace row is inserted and updated during this time.
3. The list only measures again if `onLayout` fires through react-native-web's ResizeObserver when the screen is shown again. If Safari misses or delays that callback, the rows keep their old `top` values and the next row covers the new one. Each extra workspace adds more stale positions, which fits the report that the first row is fully covered after a second create.

A second problem makes this worse. [`WorkspaceListTable/index.tsx:217`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/src/components/Tables/WorkspaceListTable/index.tsx#L217) builds row keys from the list position (`${row.policyID}-${index}`). Inserting a workspace into the sorted list therefore changes the key of every row below it.

**What I couldn't confirm:** I couldn't confirm the Safari-specific trigger. I ran the steps on web with headless Chromium and the rows did not overlap after either the first or the second create. To confirm, reproduce in Safari with Web Inspector open, go back to the Workspaces tab, and compare each FlashList cell's inline `top`/`height` with its real content height. If scrolling or resizing the window fixes the overlap, the stored layout is stale.

**Possible fix, if confirmed:**
- In `TableBody`, make the list measure again when the screen regains focus, for example by passing a focus counter from `useIsFocused` as FlashList `extraData`. Don't rely only on ResizeObserver.
- Change `keyExtractor` to `row.policyID` so that inserting a row doesn't change the keys of the rows below it.
- If neither fixes it, check whether the sticky list header added in [Keep the table column header inside the scroller on web](https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/103938) behaves differently in Safari.

---
**Next Steps:** Reply with `@MelvinBot <your feedback>` to refine this analysis.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

After creating a workspace and returning to the Workspaces tab, rows in the workspace list overlap: the row above is partially hidden underneath the row below it, and after creating one more workspace the first row can be covered completely. Reported on macOS Safari, and the broken layout persists for as long as the page stays open.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

The Workspaces page renders its rows through the shared Table component, whose body is a FlashList:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/f0422d2ce11c4dbbbf4026f44e3dcc557bff756a/src/components/Table/TableBody.tsx#L472-L479

On web, FlashList v2 absolutely positions every row: each cell wrapper gets an inline top offset computed from the stored, measured heights of the rows above it in its internal layout table. Those stored heights are collected by RecyclerView's layout effects, which synchronously measure the mounted rows' DOM boxes on each commit (in the copy of `@shopify/flash-list` we already modify via the patch `@shopify+flash-list+2.3.2+002+skip-layout-when-hidden.patch`).

When the user presses Confirm, the new policy is written optimistically and the app navigates to the new workspace's Overview screen at the same time, so the Workspaces screen is hidden with display: none by the navigation stack. The list for that screen therefore inserts and measures the new row around the hidden/visible boundary of its own screen. Our existing skip-layout-when-hidden patch guards the pipeline while the container measures 0x0, but it leaves one window open: on the commit where the screen becomes visible again (the user returns to the Workspaces tab), the layout effect synchronously reads the just-unhidden rows' boxes. Safari (the reported environment is Monterey's WebKit on slow hardware) can return a stale, too-small box for a row in that window — before the un-hidden subtree has been properly reflowed — and that wrong height is written into the layout table. The next row's top offset is then computed from the wrong stored height, which places it on top of the previous row. The report video shows exactly this geometry: the first row's layout slot is roughly half a row tall while its content still renders at full height, and the second row sits at the offset that the too-small stored height produces.

Crucially, the bad value then sticks. Stored item layouts are only corrected when a later commit re-measures the rows or when the row's ResizeObserver fires — and the ResizeObserver only reports the unhide transition itself (inside that same window); after that the row's real DOM size never changes, so no later callback arrives to correct the one-shot measurement taken at the unhide commit. That is why the overlap persists indefinitely instead of self-correcting a frame later, and why the bug is timing-dependent (it reproduces on Safari, while Chromium's reflow timing returns correct boxes in the same window).

This is the same family of hidden-while-updating layout races that our flash-list patch set already addresses (skip-layout-when-hidden, pending-children-blocking-measurements, and the two ignore-stale-viewholder-layout patches) — but none of those re-validates stored heights when the container transitions back from hidden to visible.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Extend our flash-list patch set with a follow-up to the skip-layout-when-hidden patch, in RecyclerView's layout measurement path. In the effect that measures the parent container (the one the existing patch teaches to record a 0x0 size while hidden), detect the transition from the hidden state back to a real, non-zero size. When that transition happens, schedule a single re-validation pass on the next animation frame: re-measure every mounted ViewHolder with the measurement helper the effect already uses, and feed the results through the existing child-layout modification path so stale entries in the layout table are overwritten with the rows' real heights. Deferring that pass by one frame guarantees WebKit has actually laid out the un-hidden subtree before we read its boxes, which closes the stale-measurement window that produces the overlap, and it self-heals any layout recorded incorrectly around the hidden period. The pass only runs on the hidden-to-visible transition, so steady-state scrolling and measurement behavior are untouched, and it is platform-agnostic (a no-op where measurements were already correct, like Chromium). The new patch gets an entry in the patch set's details document per convention, and should be offered upstream like the existing patches in this family.

This fixes the overlap for every FlashList-backed Table screen (workspaces, members, categories, and so on), not just the Workspaces list, since any of them can update while their screen is hidden behind a navigation.

**Compare branch:** https://github.com/Expensify/App/compare/main...wildan-m:App:wildan/104951-revalidate-flashlist-after-unhide?expand=1

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

An app-level workaround in the Workspaces list page — forcing the table to re-layout when the screen regains focus after the create flow. Rejected because the stale measurement lives in the list engine, so each Table-backed screen would need its own workaround while the underlying window stayed open; fixing it once at the patch level matches how this family of issues has been handled before.

Melvin was not able to find the correct root cause.

Opening for proposals.
Note for contributors: I won't accept any proposals without sharing repro video.

# Proposal

## Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

On the Workspaces list (web / macOS Safari), after creating a new workspace and returning to the Workspaces tab, the newly created workspace row is partially overlapped (obscured) by the row below it. Creating a second workspace makes the first row become fully hidden behind the next one. Rows in the list should each occupy their own space and render fully.

## What is the root cause of that problem?

The Workspaces list is a `FlashList` (through the shared `Table` component), and the list is given a `keyExtractor` that mixes the row's position (`index`) into its key:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/src/components/Tables/WorkspaceListTable/index.tsx#L217

This value is what actually reaches `FlashList` — `TableBody` forwards the consumer's `keyExtractor` for every data row, and passes it straight to the list:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/src/components/Table/TableBody.tsx#L431-L439

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/src/components/Table/TableBody.tsx#L497

Why that breaks: the list is sorted by workspace name (`initialSortColumn="workspaces"`), so when a new workspace is inserted it lands somewhere in the middle/top of the sorted order and shifts the index of every row after it. Because the key is `` `${row.policyID}-${index}` ``, each shifted row gets a **brand-new key** even though it is the same workspace. FlashList v2 caches each item's measured size by its key and positions items absolutely from those cached sizes; when the keys churn on every insert/reorder, the previously-measured heights are discarded and rows are temporarily laid out with estimated/average sizes. On Safari the re-measure of the real height commits late (layout/ResizeObserver timing differs from Chrome), so the stale, too-small offset is left on screen and the following row ends up painted on top of the new row. A second insertion causes more key churn and a larger offset error, so the first row is fully covered.

The row key is meant to be a **stable identity** per item, not its position. The data source already guarantees a unique, stable id per row: the selector builds exactly one entry per policy from the policy collection, and the page sets `keyForList`/`policyID` to that id for both regular and join-request rows:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/src/selectors/Policy.ts#L132-L185

Appending `index` to that already-unique id adds nothing except instability. Every other list table in the repo keys off the stable id alone (e.g. `keyExtractor={(item) => item.keyForList}`), which is the idiomatic FlashList pattern.

## What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Key each row by its stable `policyID` only, so the key no longer changes when the sorted order shifts after an insert. This lets FlashList keep each item's measured height across reorders and position rows correctly.

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/src/components/Tables/WorkspaceListTable/index.tsx#L217

```ts
keyExtractor={(row) => row.policyID}
```

`policyID` is unique per row (one entry per policy, see the selector above), so removing `index` is safe and introduces no duplicate-key risk. This matches how the rest of the list tables key their rows and follows FlashList's requirement that keys be stable identities rather than positions.

Note: `DomainListTable` (`` `${row.domainAccountID}-${index}` ``) and `WorkspaceRoomsTable` (`` `${row.reportID}-${index}` ``) use the same `id-index` pattern and are susceptible to the identical overlap on reorder/insert; they should be fixed the same way (drop the trailing `-${index}`), but they are out of scope for this issue.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

After creating a workspace and returning to the Workspaces list, the newly displayed workspace row overlaps the row beneath it. The overlap persists while navigating away and back, and is reproducible in Safari on both staging and production. The reported video demonstrates the issue: [[issue #104951](https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/104951)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/104951), [[reproduction video](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/14427be3-b97b-4c4a-b931-d1b64932bf87)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/14427be3-b97b-4c4a-b931-d1b64932bf87).

### What is the root cause of that problem?

The Workspaces list is rendered through the shared `TableBody`/FlashList implementation. Its rows are positioned using FlashList’s cached layout measurements: [[WorkspaceListTable](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/src/components/Tables/WorkspaceListTable/index.tsx#L215-L217)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/src/components/Tables/WorkspaceListTable/index.tsx#L215-L217), [[TableBody](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/src/components/Table/TableBody.tsx#L459-L498)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/src/components/Table/TableBody.tsx#L459-L498).

When the confirmation flow creates the workspace, it optimistically updates the policy data and reveals the destination route while the Workspaces list is still hidden: [[workspace confirmation flow](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/src/libs/actions/Policy/CreateWorkspaceFlow.tsx#L121-L136)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/src/libs/actions/Policy/CreateWorkspaceFlow.tsx#L121-L136), [[optimistic workspace creation](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/src/libs/actions/Policy/Policy.ts#L3359-L3368)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/src/libs/actions/Policy/Policy.ts#L3359-L3368).

The existing FlashList patch intentionally skips layout work when the parent measures `0x0`, and relies on a later visibility/layout notification to resume: [[skip-layout-when-hidden.patch](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/patches/%40shopify/flash-list/%40shopify%2Bflash-list%2B2.3.2%2B002%2Bskip-layout-when-hidden.patch#L5-L25)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/patches/%40shopify/flash-list/%40shopify%2Bflash-list%2B2.3.2%2B002%2Bskip-layout-when-hidden.patch#L5-L25), [[patch documentation](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/patches/@shopify/flash-list/details.md#L13-L29)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d138eba30e28ff0c0998ad13c1cc60bd624c9424/patches/@shopify/flash-list/details.md#L13-L29).

On Safari/WebKit, the first item measurement performed during the hidden-to-visible transition can be stale. FlashList then stores an incorrect row height/offset. Because the row’s actual DOM size does not subsequently change, no later measurement necessarily corrects the cached layout, leaving the following row positioned on top of it.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Add a follow-up FlashList patch for the hidden-to-visible transition.

- Track when the RecyclerView parent was previously measured as `0x0`.
- When it receives its first non-zero measurement after being hidden, schedule one `requestAnimationFrame` on web.
- In that frame, remeasure every mounted ViewHolder using the existing item-measurement helper.
- Pass those measurements through `modifyChildrenLayout` so cached heights and positions are corrected.
- Skip the work if the list was disposed, became hidden again, or has no layout yet.
- Cancel any pending animation frame when the RecyclerView unmounts.
- Document the new patch alongside the existing hidden-layout patch.

The revalidation should only run once after a hidden-to-visible transition, leaving steady-state FlashList measurement unchanged.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Changing the workspace row key to `policyID` alone would not address the measured-layout corruption and would risk restoring the sorting-position regression that caused the current `${policyID}-${index}` key to be introduced: [[sorting position fix](https://github.com/Expensify/App/commit/1048f8bf5ef192769c9708604e416bb810c41712)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/commit/1048f8bf5ef192769c9708604e416bb810c41712). The reproduction also shows the existing row remaining in place while the new row is added, so key changes do not explain the observed first-create overlap.

## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

I could not reproduce this on current `main` (f97c37c). With the issue's steps in WebKit 17.4 and 16.4 (the Safari engines that run on macOS Monterey) and in WebKit 26.6, every workspace row is 56px tall, at top `217` / `273` / `329`. So the root cause below is what the report's video shows plus what the code rules out. I have not confirmed the producer in a run.

<!-- ATTACH after-webkit17-main.mp4 -->

In the video, with two workspaces the second row starts exactly one row below the column header, where it belongs. The **first** row is the one that is wrong: its background fills both rows' height and its content sits about half a row lower than with one workspace. With three workspaces, a box as tall as the whole list puts its content a full row lower, under row 2. That is the "completely obscured" case.

That rules out the list positions. FlashList always places item 0 at `y = 0` and gives vertical items only a width:

https://github.com/Shopify/flash-list/blob/v2.3.2/src/recyclerview/layout-managers/LinearLayoutManager.ts#L154-L167

A cell gets a height only for `enforcedHeight`, and FlashList never sets that:

https://github.com/Shopify/flash-list/blob/v2.3.2/src/recyclerview/ViewHolder.tsx#L120

So a stale stored layout or a changed key moves rows; it cannot make row 1 taller. Row 2 also sits at the correct offset, which FlashList only computes from a correct 56px measurement of row 1.

So the producer is a style inside the first row: in the reporter's Safari build, a height in that row resolves against the list's height instead of the row's content.

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/f97c37ce20f2fc624ef3672e09ce756e04406cf8/src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx#L180-L210

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

No FlashList, `keyExtractor` or re-measure change, since none of them can stop row 1 from stretching. First I'd confirm on the latest staging with the exact Safari version. Then I'd fix the one `TableRow` style whose computed height in Web Inspector equals the list height, so the row sizes to its content (56px).

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

- Re-measuring rows after the list is shown again, or keying rows by `policyID`/index: rejected, because they only change positions and row 2's position is already correct.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

On web Safari, after creating a second workspace, the first row in the Workspaces list is partly covered by the row below it, and with a third workspace it is fully covered.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

First, what the video actually shows, because it rules out a couple of directions:

- At ~0:36 the tester goes to Troubleshoot > Clear cache and restart, the page reloads, and from ~0:40 to the end the overlap is still there in exactly the same spot. After a fresh load there is no hidden screen being measured and no workspace being inserted into the list, so this isn't a stale measurement from the hidden-to-visible transition and it isn't key churn from `${policyID}-${index}`. It's a deterministic layout result for this data in this Safari.
- Frame measurements (same crop, 1x): with one workspace the row spans y 88 to 143 (55px) and the name is centered at ~111. With two workspaces, row 2 sits exactly where it should (143 to 198), but row 1's background runs from 88 down under row 2 and its name is centered at ~138, so row 1's box is ~110px (two rows) with its content vertically centered in it. With three rows the same box is three rows tall, its content lands in the middle of row 2, and that's the "completely obscured" case.

So FlashList's offsets are right (row 2 can only be at 143 if row 1 was measured at 55). What's wrong is the painted height of row 1, which grows to the bottom of the list's items container.

FlashList positions each cell absolutely with only `top`/`left`/`width` and never a height for a vertical list:

https://github.com/Shopify/flash-list/blob/v2.3.2/src/recyclerview/ViewHolder.tsx#L116-L130

Inside that cell, the row's height is built entirely from `flex: 1` boxes plus a `minHeight`:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/b0838b269f0146f6afa0e35280ff201eceb9c284/src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx#L180-L211

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/b0838b269f0146f6afa0e35280ff201eceb9c284/src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx#L402-L412

react-native-web passes `flex: 1` through as the CSS shorthand, which is `flex: 1 1 0%`. The `0%` basis is a percentage of the parent's height, and the parent here is an absolutely positioned cell whose height is auto, so it is indefinite. Chrome treats that as content-sized. The older WebKit on Monterey resolves it against the cell's containing block instead, which is FlashList's items container (height = sum of all rows). The `flex: 1` content box then grows to the bottom of that container and the row's `alignItemsCenter` centers the content in the taller box. That's why:

- the first row grows by exactly one row per extra workspace (its top is 0, so it stretches over all rows below it)
- the last row looks fine (nothing below it to stretch over)
- later rows still paint on top of it, since they come later in DOM order

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Remove the percentage basis from the row's height chain so nothing inside the cell can resolve against the list. In `TableRow`, swap `styles.flex1` for `styles.flexGrow1` (grow with `flex-basis: auto`) on the two inner wrappers, `tableRowContentContainerStyles` and `tableRowContentStyles`:

```ts
const tableRowContentContainerStyles = [
    styles.flexGrow1,
    styles.gap3,
    animatedHighlightStyle,
    ...
];

const tableRowContentStyles = [
    styles.flexGrow1,
    styles.flexRow,
    styles.alignItemsCenter,
    ...
];
```

The row keeps its `minHeight` from `tableRowHeight`, so in every browser it still fills that height. The only difference is that the auto basis comes from content and not from a percentage of an indefinite parent, so old Safari has nothing to resolve against the items container. Native layout doesn't change, because Yoga treats `flex: 1` and `flexGrow: 1` the same way in a column without a fixed height.

This is in the shared `TableRow`, so the other Table screens with the same row structure (members, categories, rooms, domains) get the fix too.

I'd also add a short comment above the two styles so `flex1` doesn't get added back.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

- Give the FlashList cell a definite height on web via `overrideItemLayout` with the measured row height. That also stops the stretch, but it fixes the row height and breaks rows that grow, like a row with an error message or a `rowFooter`.
- Re-measuring the list when it becomes visible again, or changing the row key: these only move rows. Row 2's position is already correct, and the overlap survives a full reload, so neither one changes what's on screen.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
On macOS Safari Web, when the Workspaces list (`WorkspacesListPage` / `WorkspaceListTable`) has multiple workspaces, the first workspace row is partially obscured by the second row (with 2 workspaces) and completely obscured behind the second row (with 3 workspaces), even after clearing cache and reloading the page.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
The bug is not caused by `FlashList` hidden-screen measurement skipping (`skip-layout-when-hidden.patch`) or `keyExtractor` index churn alone, because:
1. In the reproduction video (`00:36–00:45`), the user performs **Troubleshoot > Clear cache and restart**, which reloads the page directly on the Workspaces list with no hidden-screen transition and no dynamic row insertion, yet the overlap still occurs identically.
2. In the video, Row 2 is positioned at the exact `56px` vertical offset below the table header (`FlashList` measured Row 1 at `56px`), while Row 1's background stretches across the full multi-row list height and vertically centers Row 1's content at the midpoint of the entire list—placing Row 1's text directly underneath Row 2's opaque `styles.highlightBG` background when there are 3 rows (`168px / 2 = 84px`, which lies inside Row 2's `56px..112px` box).

The root cause is in `src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx` (lines `196-215` and `407-417`):
1. `FlashList` v2 renders each vertical cell (`ViewHolder`) as an absolutely positioned container (`position: absolute; left: 0; top: <offset>px; width: 100%`) without an explicit `height` (`height: auto`).
2. Inside `TableRow.tsx`, `PressableWithFeedback` applies `rowHeightStyle` (`styles.tableRowHeight`, which only sets `minHeight`, not `height`).
3. Inside `PressableWithFeedback`, both nested wrappers use `styles.flex1` (`flex: 1 1 0%`):
   - `tableRowContentContainerStyles` (`src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx:196-203`):
     ```ts
     const tableRowContentContainerStyles = [
         styles.flex1,
         styles.gap3,
         animatedHighlightStyle,
         isLastRow && styles.tableBottomRadius,
         shouldUseNarrowTableLayout ? styles.ph4 : styles.ph3,
         rowVerticalPaddingStyle,
     ];
     ```
   - `tableRowContentStyles` (`src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx:205-215`):
     ```ts
     const tableRowContentStyles = [
         styles.flex1,
         styles.flexRow,
         styles.alignItemsCenter,
         styles.alignContentCenter,
         styles.gap3,
         styles.dFlex,
         rowContentHeightStyle,
         !shouldUseNarrowTableLayout && [styles.dGrid, {gridTemplateColumns: gridTemplateColumns.join(' ')}],
     ];
     ```
4. On Web, `react-native-web` compiles `styles.flex1` to `flex: 1 1 0%`. Because the parent cell has an indefinite `height: auto` (`minHeight` only) inside `FlashList`'s positioned items container, WebKit/Safari resolves the percentage basis (`0%`) and flex growth against the positioned containing block (`FlashList`'s total items container height) rather than content height. Consequently, Row 0 (`top: 0`) stretches to the bottom of the list container, and `styles.alignItemsCenter` / `styles.alignContentCenter` centers Row 0's cells vertically across the multi-row height right behind Row 1's opaque background.
5. Additionally, in `src/components/Tables/WorkspaceListTable/index.tsx` (line `217`), `keyExtractor={(row, index) => `${row.policyID}-${index}`}` appends the sorted array index to `policyID`, which invalidates `FlashList` key-to-height cache entries for all subsequent rows whenever a newly created workspace is inserted into alphabetical order.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
1. **Replace `styles.flex1` (`flex-basis: 0%`) with `styles.flexGrow1` (`flex-grow: 1; flex-basis: auto`) on `tableRowContentContainerStyles` and `tableRowContentStyles` in `src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx` (lines `196-215`)**:
   Using `styles.flexGrow1` keeps the `auto` flex-basis so each row sizes strictly to its content + `minHeight` (`styles.tableRowHeight`) in Safari/WebKit without resolving a `0%` percentage basis against `FlashList`'s positioned container, while still expanding to fill `minHeight` on all platforms.

```diff
diff --git a/src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx b/src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx
--- a/src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx
+++ b/src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx
@@ -194,13 +194,13 @@ export default function TableRow({
     ];
 
     const tableRowContentContainerStyles = [
-        styles.flex1,
+        styles.flexGrow1,
         styles.gap3,
         animatedHighlightStyle,
         isLastRow && styles.tableBottomRadius,
         shouldUseNarrowTableLayout ? styles.ph4 : styles.ph3,
         rowVerticalPaddingStyle,
     ];
 
     const tableRowContentStyles = [
-        styles.flex1,
+        styles.flexGrow1,
         styles.flexRow,
         styles.alignItemsCenter,
         styles.alignContentCenter,
```

2. **Use stable `row.policyID` in `WorkspaceListTable` `keyExtractor` (`src/components/Tables/WorkspaceListTable/index.tsx:217`)**:
   Change `keyExtractor={(row, index) => `${row.policyID}-${index}`}` to `keyExtractor={(row) => row.policyID}` so inserting a newly created workspace into the sorted list does not churn the keys of rows below it.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)
- Patching `@shopify/flash-list` to re-measure on `0x0` -> non-zero transitions: Rejected as the primary fix because the overlap reproduces immediately after a full page reload (`Clear cache and restart`) when the list is never `0x0`.
- Setting a fixed `height` instead of `minHeight` on `styles.tableRowHeight`: Rejected because table rows with inline `ErrorMessageRow` or `rowFooter` content must be able to grow taller than `56px`.

## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

Aura reproduced the issue on staging `9.5.28-5` using Playwright WebKit 16.4 on macOS 26.3. After creating a second and then a third workspace, the first row stayed at the same position and height. Its name moved outside it. WebKit 17.4 and 26.5 kept the name centered. The original report used retail Safari on Monterey.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a5fca5f-442b-486c-907a-e94e691441ea

Earlier proposals correctly drew attention to the first row’s contents. The wide version of `TableRow` defines grid columns but leaves the row size implicit. On the affected engine, the grid places the first name outside its own bounds. With three workspaces, the first row spanned y=217–273, but its name was centered at y=517. Giving the grid an explicit row moved the name to y=245, exactly the row center. Removing that setting moved it to y=301, where the second row covered it. The row positions stayed the same throughout. [TableRow source](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/89308067b4df3aa977c49c706a7da1cbf43a0cab/src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx#L201-L211)

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Add `gridTemplateRows: 'minmax(0, 1fr)'` alongside the existing column definition in the wide web grid. This gives the row an explicit track without hard-coding a pixel height. I’d verify that every workspace name stays inside its own clickable row after each creation, then check compact rows, wrapped content, expandable rows, and the narrow layout because `TableRow` is shared.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

In an offline replay of the staging table on WebKit 16.4, changing both inner wrappers to `flexGrow: 1` with an automatic basis left the first name outside its row. The explicit grid row centered it with the original flex styles in place.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

Rows in the Workspaces list are drawn on top of one another after creating a workspace, so the row above ends up covered by the one below it.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7006b618-58be-4795-a95e-8b5a08d712c3

Repro on Safari 16.5.1 / macOS Ventura against staging, starting from an account with no workspaces: create one workspace, return to the list, create a second, return to the list. Reading the rows back out of the DOM at each step:

```
after the first workspace    row 0   top 0    stored height 56   content needs 114
after the second workspace   row 0   top 0    stored height 56   content needs 70
                             row 1   top 56   stored height 56   content needs 56
```

Row 0 is positioned using a stored height of 56 while it actually needs more, so row 1 is painted too high and slices into it. Two runs from a clean account, same result both times.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

Two things happen at the same instant when you press Confirm: the new policy is written optimistically, so a row is inserted into the Workspaces list, and the app navigates to the new workspace's Overview, so the Workspaces screen is hidden by the navigator.

The list keys its rows by the sorted index:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/af8faeb92234f93e9e0bb22de86bb17c36959618/src/components/Tables/WorkspaceListTable/index.tsx#L207

and that value is what reaches FlashList, because `TableBody` forwards the consumer's extractor for every data row:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/af8faeb92234f93e9e0bb22de86bb17c36959618/src/components/Table/TableBody.tsx#L434

Since the list is sorted by name, inserting a workspace changes the index, and therefore the key, of every row after the insertion point. FlashList treats those as different items and replaces their view holders.

That replacement lands while the screen is hidden, and while hidden we deliberately measure nothing:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/af8faeb92234f93e9e0bb22de86bb17c36959618/patches/@shopify/flash-list/@shopify+flash-list+2.3.2+002+skip-layout-when-hidden.patch#L5-L25

Both guards return early when the container is 0x0: the first skips measuring the container, the second skips collecting layout info for the mounted view holders. Rows on web are absolutely positioned from the heights stored in that layout table, so the rows that were just replaced keep whatever offsets were stored before, and the newly inserted one has never been measured at all.

The part that makes it stick is that nothing runs the skipped pass again. The early return records no pending work, so when the screen is shown again the layout is only corrected if `onLayout` happens to fire through react-native-web's ResizeObserver. When it does not, the stale `top` values survive and a row is painted over its neighbour.

Starting from an empty account is what makes it easy to hit. The first workspace is the default one, so its row carries the `Default` badge and is taller than a plain row, while the layout table still holds the height it was given before anyone measured it. Creating another workspace repeats the cycle, which matches the report that the first row ends up completely covered the second time.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Make the skip recoverable instead of silent, in `@shopify+flash-list+2.3.2+002+skip-layout-when-hidden.patch`.

When either guard returns early because the container is 0x0, set a flag on the recycler view recording that a layout pass was skipped while hidden. Then, where the container size is next observed to be non zero, if that flag is set, clear it and run the pass that was skipped: measure the currently mounted view holders and feed the result through the normal `modifyLayout` path so the positions are recomputed from the first index whose height changed. That restores the invariant the patch broke, which is that every mount is eventually measured, without giving up the thing the patch was added for, which is not measuring while the size is 0x0.

This is deliberately in the patch rather than in `WorkspaceListTable`, because the hidden then shown sequence is not specific to workspaces. Any table that is mutated while its screen sits behind another one can land in the same state.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Keying the rows by `policyID` alone, so that inserting a workspace does not change the identity of every row below it and no view holders are replaced. This removes the trigger rather than the fault, and it needs care: the index was added to the key to fix row positioning when sorting, so the sort behaviour has to be preserved through the data order instead of through the key. I would treat it as a complement to the fix above rather than a replacement, since the underlying skipped measurement would still be reachable by other means.

## Proposal ### What is the root cause of that problem? The rows are in the right place, but the first row's cells are drawn too low, behind the row below it. It's a Safari layout issue in the shared table row, not a measuring or key problem. Each row lays out its cells in a CSS grid (`display: grid`, `align-content: center`), and that grid also gets `flex: 1` so it grows to fill the row: https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ab0251e86bdd66e0ff0d819b8b1567508e057051/src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx#L201-L211 FlashList puts every row in an absolutely positioned cell with an auto height. In Safari 17.5, the first row's growing grid keeps its 40px box but centers its cells in the height of the whole list. I measured it in Safari 17.5 (iPad simulator, iOS 17.5, landscape) with 3 workspaces: - The first row's grid box is 40px tall, but its cells start 70px below the row's top, under row 2. In the other rows they start at 15px. - With `align-content: normal`, the first row's grid track becomes 152px: the list's 168px (3 × 56px) minus the row's 16px padding. The other rows get 39px. That matches the report: half covered with 2 workspaces, fully with 3. It also shows on a plain page load (my runs open Workspaces directly, with no workspace created in that session). And it isn't limited to Workspaces: in the same Safari, the first row of the Categories table ("Advertising") is blank too. ### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem? Stop the grid from growing. `rowContentHeightStyle` already gives it the row's min height (39px), so it doesn't need `flex: 1`: ```diff const tableRowContentStyles = [ - styles.flex1, styles.flexRow, styles.alignItemsCenter, ``` I ran each change in Safari 17.5 with 3 workspaces: | Change | First row in Safari 17.5 | |---|---| | main | blank (cells at 70px) | | `flexGrow: 1` instead of `flex: 1` on both wrappers | still blank (70px) | | no grow on the grid (this change) | shown (14px), in Workspaces and Categories | In Chrome nothing moves except the first row's cells, 0.5px up (that row has no top border, so `flex: 1` was giving it 1px). The narrow layout is unchanged in Chrome and Safari 17.5. Safari 27.0.1 doesn't show the bug on main. `TableTest` and `TableSelectionTest` pass (77 tests). Safari 17.5: staging first, then my local build with the change: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2003d6f5-334c-40fb-99d5-b819547f6258 Workspaces and Categories, main (top) and with the change (bottom): To reproduce without Monterey: Xcode's iOS 17.5 simulator, iPad Pro in landscape, Safari, staging, an account with 2 or more workspaces (I used 3). Not tested: macOS Monterey itself (iPadOS 17.5 has the same WebKit version), Safari 15 or 16, and the native apps. ### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional) - **`flexGrow: 1` instead of `flex: 1`:** still blank (table above), so the `0%` basis isn't the cause. - **An explicit grid row (`gridTemplateRows: 'minmax(0, 1fr)'`):** also fixes Safari 17.5 in my test. I prefer dropping `flex: 1` because it does nothing else here: the min height already sizes every row, and `flex: 1` only adds 1px to the first row. So the fix deletes the trigger instead of adding a rule to hold it back. - **A fixed height on FlashList's cell:** also fixes it, but rows that grow (an error message or a footer) would spill into the next row. - **A top border on the first row too** (it's the only row without one): still blank (cells at 71px), so the missing border isn't the cause. - **`align-content: start`:** no overlap, but every row's content moves 6px up. - **Re-measuring the list after it was hidden, or stable row keys:** the row tops are already 56px apart (217, 273, 329) in my readout, so neither would change it.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
On MacOS Safari, after a workspace is created and the Workspaces list is shown again, the new row is partly covered by the workspace row below it. Creating another workspace covers the row above it the same way. The rows should be fully visible.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
The wide row content is a CSS grid and a growing flex item. `flex: 1` is the shorthand `flex: 1 1 0%`, and `align-content: center` is set on the same view. The row itself only has a minimum height.

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/b0838b269f0146f6afa0e35280ff201eceb9c284/src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx#L201-L211

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/b0838b269f0146f6afa0e35280ff201eceb9c284/src/styles/utils/flex.ts#L17-L19

That grid sits in a column container that also grows. The only other children of the container are the row footer and the error row, and both come after the grid.

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/b0838b269f0146f6afa0e35280ff201eceb9c284/src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx#L192-L199

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/b0838b269f0146f6afa0e35280ff201eceb9c284/src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx#L403-L423

None of these boxes has a definite height. The pressable's minimum is 56px, and the grid's minimum is 56 minus the 16px of vertical padding and the 1px top border, which is 39. The first row has no top border, so its content box is 40px.

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/b0838b269f0146f6afa0e35280ff201eceb9c284/src/styles/index.ts#L2903-L2917

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/b0838b269f0146f6afa0e35280ff201eceb9c284/src/styles/variables.ts#L194-L196

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/b0838b269f0146f6afa0e35280ff201eceb9c284/src/components/Table/TableRow.tsx#L186

Safari 16 lays the growing grid's tracks out against a larger height taken from the list cell's containing block, then clamps the grid's border box back to its 39px minimum. `align-content: center` places the cells in that larger box. The owner cell is the lowest one, so it paints below the row, and the next row starts at the measured 56px border box and covers it. The measured content height followed the list's stored size: 114px for one row, and 214px for two rows while the list still used its 200px estimate. The owner's top was that content height minus the 28px avatar.

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/b0838b269f0146f6afa0e35280ff201eceb9c284/src/components/Tables/WorkspaceListTable/WorkspaceTableRow.tsx#L198-L211

The grow is what triggers it. Keeping a grow of 1 and only changing the basis to `auto` still overlaps. Removing the grow does not. The grow also has no free space to fill: a footer or an error can only make the container taller, and on a normal bordered row the free space is exactly the 39px minimum. Current Chrome sizes the grid from its content. The narrow layout never applies this grid.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
Stop the wide web grid from growing. A platform-split helper returns grow 0, shrink 0, and basis `auto` on web, which is the view's own default and overrides `flex: 1`. The native file returns nothing, so a wide native row keeps `flex: 1`. The helper is added only inside the wide-grid style array. React Native Web puts the `flex` shorthand in an earlier style group than the longhands, so the longhands win.

The first wide web row has no top border, so its content minimum is raised by that 1px, from 39 to 40. That is the only pixel the grow was filling on a browser that already laid the row out correctly. Group headers and the narrow layout do not take this branch.

```diff
+ const wideRowFirstContentHeightStyle =
+     Platform.OS === 'web' && !shouldUseNarrowTableLayout && !isGroupHeader && isFirstRow && typeof rowContentHeightStyle?.minHeight === 'number'
+         ? {minHeight: rowContentHeightStyle.minHeight + variables.borderTopWidth}
+         : undefined;

  styles.dFlex,
  rowContentHeightStyle,
+ wideRowFirstContentHeightStyle,
  !shouldUseNarrowTableLayout && [styles.dGrid, getWideRowContentGrowStyle(styles), {gridTemplateColumns: gridTemplateColumns.join(' ')}],
```

```diff
function getWideRowContentGrowStyle(styles): ViewStyle[] | undefined {
-    return undefined;
+    return [styles.flexGrow0, styles.flexShrink0, styles.flexBasisAuto];
}
```

The second snippet is the web file. The native file keeps the `undefined` return.

On Monterey Safari 16.6, creating three workspaces leaves every name, Default badge, and owner inside its row. In current Chrome, the wide rows in Workspaces, Categories, Members, Rooms, and Distance rates keep the same grid height and the same cell tops, including the first row and the selection checkboxes. The row menu is a popover, so this change does not affect it.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)
Giving the grid a fixed 39px height and `overflow: hidden` contains the paint, but it clips a cell that is taller than the row instead of placing it correctly.

`grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)` also keeps the cells inside the row on Safari 16. The `1fr` track is still sized from the same stretched height, and the `0` minimum can squeeze a taller cell.

Deleting `flex: 1` from the shared content style fixes the wide web row and also changes narrow rows and native rows. The first row then sits 0.5px higher, because that shared deletion removes the 1px the first row was growing into.

Remeasuring the FlashList cell, or storing a taller row height, only moves the next row. The owner cell still paints below the 56px border box.

### What specific scenarios should we cover in automated tests?
- On a wide web row, the content grid's computed flex grow is 0 and its flex basis is `auto`.
- The first wide web row's content minimum is 40px, and a later row's content minimum stays 39px.
- A narrow row and a native wide row keep `flex: 1` on that content view.
- A group header does not get the first-row minimum.
- On Safari 16, the owner cell's bottom is inside the first row's border box, and the next row starts at that border.

### Repro steps

1. On MacOS Monterey, open Safari 16 and go to https://staging.new.expensify.com/.
2. Sign in with a new account.
3. Open the Workspaces tab. The window needs to be wide enough that the list shows the Workspaces, Owner, and Workspace type columns.
4. Click + New, then Confirm.
5. Open the Workspaces tab again.
6. The new row is partly covered by the row below it. Create one more workspace and return to the list: the row above the newest one is covered the same way.
